headline: Neural decoders are judged on generalization; mechanistic claims remain untested
label: Neural Decoding Validity
summary: Recent EEG and neural decoding preprints test transfer, adaptation and cross-subject generalization, but few establish mechanistic grounds.
synthesis: The common thread is how far predictive performance in EEG and neural decoding extends beyond the conditions in which it was measured. ReBrain transfers an intracranial EEG prior to scalp recordings without paired data or fine-tuning, and reports improved downstream clinical analysis. AMRT reports cross-subject generalization for continuous motor decoding through a shared two-stage design. The BCI adaptation study frames updating frozen EEG encoders as a resource-priced decision, with gated Bayesian heads. The EEG-video study is the most explicit on validity: contrastive alignment outperforms CCA across subjects and seen stimuli but not novel videos, and a sham control shows that accuracy can be spurious. What is new across these preprints is the attention to transfer, adaptation cost and controls. None of the items tests a causal or mechanistic account, so mechanistic validity remains an open question.
